expected_level_description: You can: - monitor the analysis of a technical solution and ensure analysis is reused for similar problem sets - review solutions and identify areas for change - drive the collection of information that is used and analysed - feed back on policy and requirements

You can: - demonstrate a deep understanding of security concepts and can apply them to a technical level - effectively translate and accurately communicate security and risk implications to technical and non-technical stakeholders - successfully respond to challenges - manage stakeholder expectations and be flexible, adapting to stakeholder reactions to reach consensus
You can: - design and review system architectures through the development of patterns and principles
You can: - work with higher impact or more complex risks, advising on the impact and whether it's within risk tolerance - apply different risk methodologies in proportion to the risk

You can: - contribute to and inform developments on security properties in technology - identify new technologies and design the use of these in the business context across the organisation - engage with the broader security community
You can: - explain complex system architectures - identify and explain how easy or difficult it will be to exploit vulnerabilities - lead and influence security technology in the security industry
You can: - interpret and apply understanding across a complex area - start influencing policy and process, business architecture, and legal and political implications

You can: - analyse how a service fits into care pathways across organisations - work with clinicians, care staff, and patients to shape digital services - explain the effect of digital decisions on care, safety, and staff workload

You can: - lead data protection impact assessments and information sharing agreements - advise teams on lawful basis, consent, confidentiality, and retention - investigate incidents and recommend improvements
You can: - set the identity and access strategy for staff, patients, and systems - lead the adoption of new identity standards
You can: - prioritise vulnerabilities by risk, including to patient services - scope and manage penetration tests and remediation
You can: - monitor alerts and triage them using runbooks - gather evidence and escalate events - tune simple detection rules under guidance
You can: - take part in hazard workshops and contribute to a hazard log - follow the clinical risk management process for your work - provide evidence for a clinical safety case, such as test results
You can: - run the risk process for a directorate or programme - assess risks against the risk appetite and escalate them - report on risks to committees
You can: - line manage a team, setting objectives and running appraisals - support wellbeing and manage attendance, performance, and conduct - plan the team's development and succession
